items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: With Collective Black Artists there was Reggie Workman, there was Buster Williams

ctx.x: Exactly that. And so I mean I was doing a bunch of these big bands and all of this was in different music. Every band I went in had different musicians. So every one of these bands had a little clique of musicians that were working the bands. So I was going between about three or four different cliques in New York, so I knew a whole bevy of musicians, all of which played different from each other. So I got a chance to see sides of New York that many trumpet players never got a chance to see because they would be…
Right. Did you get the sense, when you were playing ensemble tuba, did the bass player in that group need to do any adjusting in their note choices?
